newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Re says M&G buy to boost profits.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Re says M&G buy to boost profits.

text.p: Swiss Reinsurance Co. said its acquisition of Mercantile & General Re from Britain's Prudential Corp for around 3.15 billion Swiss francs to contribute substantially to its earnings and support its goal of a 15 percent return on equity (ROE).
Swiss Re said the purchase of M&G was still subject to regulatory approval. Swiss Re intends to combine the operating activities of the two companies under Swiss Re's name.
Adding the gross premiums of M&G in 1995 of 2.4 billion Swiss francs to the 12.9 billion of Swiss Re, total premium will rise to 15.3 billion of which life and health represents 4.1 billion.
"This acquisition advances Swiss Re's strategic aim of growing its business in the life and health sector," it said.
Following the acquisition of Alhermij, the Dutch reinsurer last year, the transaction will make Swiss Re the largest life and health insurer and reinforce its worldwide leadership role.
M&G's business is complimentary to Swiss Re's strong presence in mainland Europe and in particular strengthens its business in the United States, United Kingdom and Asia/Pacific.
